text: hey everybody the Town mode has some pretty fascinating discussions about gender that I think might surprise some folks for instance we have two creation
accounts at the beginning of Genesis and the rabbis harmonize these in a few different ways and there's some rabbis who harmonize them by understanding
Genesis 1 verses 26 and 27 to be describing the creation of Adam the human as both male and female as a
single entity with a male half and a female half and then Genesis 2 describes the woman
being taken from one of the sides of the man in other words our single entity with a male and female half is divided
into two separate entities of man and a woman and while this would seem to describe a pretty clear gender binary the rabbis knew that that's not how
things always shook out in reality and So within the talmud there are six additional gender identities that are
developed in order to allow people to know precisely what legal rights and responsibilities and restrictions any
given person may have and so in addition to the traditional male and female gender identities there is an
androgynous identity which is someone who is born with both male and female sexual characteristics there is the tomb
tomb which is someone who does not clearly have either male or female sexual characteristics and then we have
the ILO Needham which is someone who is assigned female at Birth but does not develop the expected secondary sexual
characteristics at puberty because of natural causes and the ILO need Adam who is the person who is assigned female at
Birth but does not develop those characteristics at puberty because of some kind of human intervention and then there's the male counterpart the saris
the person assigned male at Birth who does not develop those characteristics because of natural causes and the saris Adam who does not develop those
characteristics because of some kind of human intervention and the rights and duties that these different identities
are assigned are some kind of mix of those assigned to men and those assigned to women but it seems to me that they probably have more restrictions placed
on them than privileges here is a list of the eight gender identities that are discussed throughout the talmud apart from males and females
some of these other non-binary identities are discussed over a hundred times in the talmud and for further discussion you can look on
